title: Whole-Wheat Blueberry Waffles
excerpt: Make whole-wheat waffles that are crisp outside and fluffy inside, full of juicy blueberries that burst with flavor in every bite. The perfect, natural breakfast to treat the family.
imageAlt: Golden, crisp whole-wheat waffles served on a ceramic plate with fresh blueberries on top and a drizzle of honey falling gently.
steps: In a large bowl, mix the dry ingredients very well: the whole-wheat flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt.
In another bowl, whisk the egg yolks with the milk, melted butter and honey. Separately, beat the egg whites to soft peaks.
Pour the liquid ingredients over the dry ones and combine gently. Then fold in the beaten whites with folding movements to keep the air in the batter. Let it rest for 5 minutes.
Preheat the waffle iron and lightly grease it with a little butter or oil.

Pour a portion of batter into the waffle iron and scatter a generous handful of Fresh Pick blueberries over it. With these high-mountain fruits grown in Guasca, their natural sweetness of 13° to 15° Brix will caramelize deliciously with the heat.
Close the waffle iron and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, or until the waffle is golden and crisp outside. Repeat with the rest of the batter.
Serve the waffles right away, topped with more fresh blueberries and an extra drizzle of honey to taste.
tips: To keep the freshness and the delicate natural protective coating (bloom) of Fresh Pick blueberries, avoid washing them ahead of time; do it only with cold water right before placing them on the batter.
Adding the blueberries straight into the waffle iron over the batter, instead of mixing them in the bowl, makes sure they are perfectly distributed in each waffle and don’t break while mixing.
If you have leftover waffles, you can freeze them in an airtight bag. To eat them later, just warm them in the toaster for a couple of minutes and they will recover their original crisp texture.
